verdict_summary: All 14 RC changes are present in the text and all 14 gate conditions from critique 01 are now met. Internal consistency passes: 43 reportable slots, no orphan, no unreachable folder. What blocks approval is five splice artefacts left by the scripted application of the edits, and one loophole in a section no RC was aimed at. Two are material: §3 still says 'Three to five images per slot' for Morrowind while §5e says 'Two to three' (RC11 was applied to §5e only), which silently reverses the largest feasibility cut in the document; and §11 rung 4 still authorises extracting a frame from video for any slot, three sections after §3 says 'Never extract a frame from a video into refs/modern/'. The other four are an unterminated code fence that swallows 80 lines including all of §8b/8c/8d, and three tables where a spliced row carries one cell too many (two of those caused by my own replacement text at RC8 and RC9). Six literal edits, no new research required.

splice_damage.location: §8a, line 327 opens; no closing fence before line 411
splice_damage.detail: Fences in v3 sit at lines 80, 101, 327, 375 (```json) and 411. The RC3 replacement consumed the closing fence that followed the old block_score definition and did not restore it. Under CommonMark/GFM a closing fence may not carry an info string, so ```json at 375 does not close the block. The code block therefore runs 328-410 and swallows §8a's rejection instruction, §8a's do-not-estimate clause, ALL of §8b (the anti-AI commit gate), §8c, §8d, and §9's opening line plus the entire MANIFEST exemplar - rendered as monospace with every ** inert, introduced by the sentence 'It walks every file and produces, per file, without you typing any of it:'. An agent taking that framing at face value reads §8b as a field description rather than a rejection rule.

splice_damage.detail: §5e (RC11) says 'Two to three images per slot' with four to five for the five core rows. §3 L135-136 still says 'Three to five images per slot'. RC11 targeted §5e's opening line only, and §3 carries a duplicate statement of the same rule. §3 is the section headed 'How many, and how to choose them', which is where an agent looks for a count. substitution_ladder_review.why_it_was_missed: §11 was added in commit b07f064, after review 02 was written and before v3's edits were applied. None of RC1-RC14 was aimed at it, and it was drafted against the looser v2 text that RC1 and RC4 subsequently tightened into absolute rules.

leaks.name: rung 4 readmits video frames to refs/modern/
leaks.detail: §11 L469-471 permits 'A frame extracted from video' for any slot, and every §5a slot lands in refs/modern/. This contradicts rule 1 (L34, no re-encode, commit the exact bytes), rule 5 (L45, 'never cut from a video') and §3 L127 ('Never extract a frame from a video into refs/modern/'). Nothing downstream catches it: §8a's block_score > 1.15 rejection carries the escape hatch 'unless nothing better exists for that slot', and rung 4's own precondition is 'only if no still exists', so the two clauses chain and the file is kept; §8b is satisfied by the video channel as 'first-party'. This is exactly ND1/ND14, the defect RC1 exists to close.

leaks.name: degraded files still count toward the §3 floors
leaks.detail: Nothing in §3, §10 or §11 excludes a file marked pixel_metrics_valid: false or heavily_recompressed: true from the per-folder count. A folder holding three video frames reports 12 against a floor of 12, §10's count table - 'the first thing we will read' - reads PASS, and the abort rule at RC2 never fires, while the population the band is computed from is 9. Worse than an honest shortfall, because the shortfall becomes invisible.

leaks.name: rungs 1 and 2 are unscoped
leaks.detail: 'Same requirement, different game. The profile matters more than the title' is written for §5a and illustrated with an Elden Ring example, but nothing limits it to REF-M slots. Applied to a REF-A slot it authorises a non-Morrowind image into refs/morrowind/, the axis-mixing failure §1 calls fatal; read strictly it could also admit an older game into refs/modern/. Partly self-defending via §7's vanilla tests (grass, distant land, cast shadows, texture resolution), but 'partly' is not the standard for the rule the folder layout exists to enforce.

does_not_leak: Modded Morrowind: barred explicitly at L489, 'Never trade vanilla-ness for image quality in that folder.'
Uncorroborated images: no rung admits one; rung 5 'leave it empty and say so' is the correct terminal.
Rehosted images: §11 is silent and does not override §4's provenance_chain rule.

feasibility.conditional_on: SD2 being fixed. As v3 literally reads, with §3 L135 governing, it is NOT achievable.
notes: Review 02 projected ~109 after cuts. The real figure is higher because RC9 added two Morrowind slots that were not in that arithmetic - a cost I asked for knowingly and the right trade, since A18 and A19 are the only anchors for the declared dusk/night palette targets and for the stilted-village vocabulary.

116-137 with the priority ladder at L56 and the abort rule at §10 is workable in one pass. 125-165 is the same over-ask review 02 ruled infeasible, concentrated in the most expensive block in the document.

Three things protect a partial run: RC5's folder priority ladder means it is partial in the right order; RC2's abort rule means a run that cannot reach the floors says so instead of padding; RC20(c) means the count table cannot report PASS on a folder padded with unmeasurable files.

NO FURTHER CUTS RECOMMENDED. Specifically do not lower the six modern floors - they are the only numbers in the document with a statistical justification, and lowering them defeats the acquisition rather than making it cheaper.

Workload note, not a defect: RC1 requires half of interior_darkemissive (5 images) to come from an interval-sampled native screenshot series, and screenshot albums skew heavily to exteriors, making that the tightest single constraint in §3. Satisfiable - a dungeon or underground run supplies it, and §6's light-decides-folder lets one run's frames distribute across all three interval-sampled folders - but expect it to be the folder that reports short.

remaining_changes.replacement_text:
(a) REPLACE §11 rung 4:

4. **A frame extracted from video — for `refs/morrowind/`, `anti-generic/` and `context/` only.**
   **Never for `refs/modern/`.** §3 forbids it absolutely there: extracting a frame encodes a new
   file, which breaks rule 1 and §4, and every frame of a compressed video carries the codec
   artefacts §8a rejects. For a REF-M slot, skip this rung and go straight to rung 5. Where it is
   allowed, mark `"provenance_chain": "video-frame"` and `"pixel_metrics_valid": false` — such a
   file is usable for composition, palette and design language only.

(b) ADD after rung 5:

**The ladder changes the subject, never the standard.** A substituted file is still subject to §4
(exact bytes, original rather than re-host), §7 (all seven vanilla tests for anything in
`refs/morrowind/`), §8a (the same automatic rejections at the same thresholds) and §8b (the same
three-way corroboration gate). Rungs 1 and 2 mean a different *current-generation* game for a
REF-M slot — never an older one — and for a REF-A slot they never mean a game other than
Morrowind: a REF-A slot that cannot be filled with vanilla Morrowind goes to rung 5, not to
another title.

(c) ADD to §3 beneath the floors table:

**Only files with `"pixel_metrics_valid": true` count toward these floors.** A video frame, or a
file the script kept but marked `"heavily_recompressed": true`, may be retained for composition and
design language but does not count toward the number in this table. A folder padded to its floor
with files we cannot measure is worse than a folder honestly reported short: the count table in
§10 reads PASS, the abort rule never fires, and the band computed from it looks exactly like a
real one.
remaining_changes.why: The §11 loophole. Rung 4 as written authorises for every REF-M slot precisely what §3 L127, rule 1 and rule 5 forbid, and the §8a 'unless nothing better exists' escape hatch chains with rung 4's 'only if no still exists' so nothing downstream catches the result. (c) closes the second half of the same problem: without it a folder padded with unmeasurable files reports PASS and the abort rule never fires.

remaining_changes.replacement_text:
- **Record how you got it.** `"provenance_chain": "original"` if you downloaded the file from the
  page that first published it; `"rehosted"` if the only reachable copy was a mirror, a Reddit or
  imgur re-post, or a wiki upload of somebody else's screenshot. Rehosted copies are acceptable and
  count toward the §3 floors provided they pass §8a — §8a is what protects calibration, and a
  re-host that passes it is measurement-identical to the original. Mark them honestly anyway, so we
  can re-check that subset first if a band later looks strange.
remaining_changes.why: My own RC10 text said rehosted files 'are not used for band calibration', which is stricter than the rest of the document and stricter than necessary: what threatens calibration is re-encoding and downscaling, and §8a measures both directly. As written it discards usable data for a provenance reason §8a has already settled, and it sits awkwardly beside RC20(c). NON-GATING - the failure mode is losing good data, not admitting bad data - but apply it while you are in the file.

what_is_good_in_v3: §8a is now a real specification. upscale_test went from a circular sentence to a procedure implementable in six lines of numpy, with a typical band and a threshold. The hardest single change asked for, and it landed exactly.
§8b is a commit gate again, with three routes rather than one, and the per-series clause removes roughly thirty redundant searches without weakening provenance at all.

RC1 solved a problem I posed badly. I identified that the anti-curation rule was unobeyable; the resolution - scope it to three folders, require native screenshot series, exempt the three folders where an unbiased run is incoherent, forbid video frames outright - is cleaner than the constraint I described.
The priority ladder at L56 and the abort rule at §10 are together what make a partial run a usable result rather than a wasted one.
RC12's paragraph on the deliberate M8 gap prevents a whole class of future damage for two lines of prose.
bottom_line: Six literal edits stand between this document and a green light. Two matter - the Morrowind count contradiction in §3 and §11 rung 4 - and four are splice tidy-up, two of which repair my own replacement text from review 02. Apply RC15-RC21, re-read §3 and §11 side by side once to confirm they agree, and this is ready to run. Nothing left to research and nothing left to argue about.
